title: Renal collecting-system injury: observation versus intervention
fairness: The resident must interpret delayed opacification through the pelvis, ureter and bladder together with a calyceal leak, then decide whether urinary extravasation warrants immediate drainage or repair. The stable course and absence of a growing or infected collection favor observation. Automatic stenting for any urine leak is a credible close error, making this moderate two-step application rather than merely identifying the known leak.

Monitored nonoperative renal care is the single best offered initial plan. The described small calyceal leak, downstream opacification, preserved perfusion and stable hemoglobin do not establish a need for immediate ureteral stenting or renal exploration. No confident clinical inaccuracy was identified in the key or explanation. Downstream opacification should not be generalized into proof that every possible partial urinary-tract injury is excluded; in this candidate it is interpreted alongside the explicitly localized calyceal injury.
